concepts.name: Market Structure
concepts.definition: Framework for reading swing highs, swing lows and directional sequences. The playbook uses higher-timeframe structure for context before lower-timeframe execution.
howToUse: Mark meaningful confirmed Monthly/Weekly/Daily swings.
Identify the latest structural break and displacement leg.
Use 4H/1H to refine context; do not let a 1M fluctuation redefine daily bias.
concepts.useCase: Use a pre-defined swing-selection rule and keep it consistent.
concepts.commonMistakes: Swing selection is discretionary unless the lookback and close rule are specified.

concepts.sourceNote: The supplied PDF is the source for playbook framing where explicitly marked. Supplemental clarifications are identified as such. These are discovery links, not verified video-to-concept mappings.

concepts.name: Swing High & Swing Low
concepts.definition: Local turning points used to map structure. The exact pivot lookback is a rule that must be fixed.
howToUse: Choose a pivot rule, such as a three-candle pivot or fixed left/right lookback.
Wait for pivot confirmation if your rule requires future candles.
Use meaningful swings for BOS/MSS, not every small fluctuation.
concepts.useCase: Mark pivots consistently and distinguish internal from major external swings.
concepts.commonMistakes: Do not select a swing retrospectively only because it makes a setup look cleaner.

concepts.name: Break of Structure (BOS)
concepts.definition: A break of a prior structural swing in the direction of the existing trend. It is a continuation clue, not an automatic entry.
howToUse: Define the swing level before the break.
Decide whether a wick or candle-body close qualifies.
Check displacement and the next liquidity pool.
concepts.useCase: Use BOS to describe continuation context after a structural level is broken.
concepts.commonMistakes: A wick through a minor pivot is not automatically a meaningful BOS.

concepts.name: Market Structure Shift (MSS)
concepts.definition: A break through a relevant swing opposite to prior short-term structure, ideally with displacement. In the playbook, MSS confirms after a liquidity raid.
howToUse: Identify prior short-term structure.
Wait for a close through the opposing swing under a fixed rule.
Assess displacement and imbalance.
Only then evaluate a pullback entry.
concepts.useCase: Use MSS after a meaningful level is reached or liquidity is swept.
concepts.commonMistakes: Do not treat every small lower-timeframe break as a reversal; the PDF distinguishes MSS from CHoCH terminology.

concepts.name: Displacement
concepts.definition: A fast directional move with relatively large candle bodies that breaks a meaningful swing and may leave imbalances. The PDF says the threshold is discretionary.
howToUse: Look for directional candles with large bodies and limited overlap.
Check whether the move closes beyond a meaningful swing.
Check for FVG/imbalance.
Define body-size, ATR or lookback filters before testing.
concepts.useCase: Use as evidence behind a structure shift, not a stand-alone direction forecast.
concepts.commonMistakes: News spikes can create movement without a durable setup.

concepts.name: Liquidity
concepts.definition: In ICT terminology, liquidity refers to orders or stops thought to cluster around obvious highs, lows and reference levels. The playbook uses pools to frame draw on liquidity.
howToUse: Mark prior highs/lows, equal highs/lows and session extremes.
Separate target pool from trigger.
Ask which untouched external level aligns with higher-timeframe narrative.
concepts.useCase: Use as a map of potential objectives, not proof that stops are visible or guaranteed to be taken.
concepts.commonMistakes: Do not assume every equal high/low must be swept.

concepts.name: Buy-Side Liquidity (BSL)
concepts.definition: A label for potential buy stops and breakout orders above visible highs. The playbook places BSL above equal highs and prior/session highs.
howToUse: Mark obvious highs and equal highs.
Treat the area above as a potential objective.
Wait for price behaviour; a sweep does not mean reversal.
concepts.useCase: Identify upside objectives and possible buy-side raids.

concepts.name: Sell-Side Liquidity (SSL)

howToUse: Mark obvious lows and equal lows.
Treat the area below as a potential downside objective.
Observe rejection versus acceptance below.

concepts.name: Liquidity Sweep / Raid

concepts.name: Fair Value Gap (FVG)
concepts.definition: Three-candle price imbalance. Bullish: candle 3 low is above candle 1 high. Bearish: candle 3 high is below candle 1 low. It is an entry zone in some models, not a signal by itself.
howToUse: Identify first and third candles.
For bullish, mark candle 1 high to candle 3 low; reverse for bearish.
Mark 50% CE if used.
Define wick-touch versus body-close mitigation/invalidation.
concepts.useCase: Require liquidity, displacement, structure and an active window as context.
concepts.commonMistakes: The PDF reports no robust proof that FVGs outperform equal-sized random zones; fills are not guaranteed.

concepts.name: FVG + OTE Confluence Model
concepts.definition: A confluence idea that looks for an FVG overlapping the 62%–79% retracement band of a defined impulse leg. The supplied playbook highlights 70.5% as a common reference.
howToUse: Select the impulse leg using a consistent structural rule.
Mark the 62%–79% retracement band and the 70.5% reference.
Identify FVG boundaries from the displacement move.
Check overlap, higher-timeframe location and session context.
Define the stop beyond the swing/raid extreme and target opposing liquidity.
concepts.useCase: Use only when impulse anchors and retracement rules are objective and repeatable.
concepts.commonMistakes: Moving Fibonacci anchors to force overlap; treating confluence as statistical proof; overlooking news and contract rollover.
